candidate.title: Latent-error momentum discriminator
candidate.one_sentence_claim: Use JEPA latent prediction error as a direct discriminator for daily return direction.
candidate.conventional_core: finance forecasting baseline with explicit abstention or targeting control
candidate.atypical_injection: report-only matched-count baseline against the approved finance snapshot
candidate.mechanism: Prediction misses may encode underreacted state transitions rather than pure representation error.
candidate.inefficiency: Papers report latent-quality gains without settling whether the error itself is decision-useful.
candidate.counterparty: Traders who anchor on reconstruction quality rather than realized signal decay.
candidate.persistence: Any link could persist while model and market microstructure remain stable.
candidate.capacity: Crowds may compress the signal once many desks trade the same error threshold.
candidate.regime_dependence: Most exposed when regime changes make representation misspecification more informative.
candidate.differential_prediction: Error-threshold portfolios should separate forward returns from matched latent-fidelity controls.
candidate.cheapest_falsifier: Compare latent-error thresholding with size-matched random and lagged-error controls.
candidate.kill_criteria: Kill if error buckets fail to improve directional separation or risk-adjusted returns.
candidate.paraphrase: JEPA latent prediction error may act as a daily return discriminator when the model underfits state shifts.

candidate_artifact.axiom: prediction error is not a sufficient forward-return discriminator

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.
